transcript: Honestly I don't really have many disagreements, I'm quite easy to work with. But okay, there was one time a colleague, another backend developer, wanted to use a different database library than the one I had already started with. His reason was it was more modern or something. I had already written a lot of code with mine, so changing would waste time. We argued about it in a meeting and I explained my side. He didn't really have strong reasons, I think he just liked the new thing. In the end the tech lead said we should keep mine because the code was already written, so, you know, it was resolved. After that we didn't talk about it again. In these situations it's important to be confident in your decisions. If you change your mind every time someone has a new idea, nothing gets built. I stayed calm and professional the whole time. He was a bit annoyed but that's normal, not everyone agrees all the time. We still worked on the same team for a while after that until I left the company.
